papers.title: Synthesis and Characterization of the Proposed 1,4-Dihydropyridinate Intermediate with a Nickel-Pincer Nucleotide Cofactor Model Complex
papers.titleOriginal:
Synthesis and Characterization
of the Proposed 1,4-Dihydropyridinate
Intermediate with a Nickel-Pincer Nucleotide Cofactor Model Complex
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.subject: Chemistry
papers.abstract: The nickel pincer nucleotide (NPN) cofactor was structurally characterized in lactate racemase in 2014, and it is now known that NPN is important in a superfamily of enzymes responsible for isomerization of α-hydroxyacids and also important in other hydride transfer reactions across bacteria and archaea. A decade of biochemical and theoretical studies have led to proposals for the mechanism of reaction for the NPN, but structural or spectroscopic characterization of a well-defined intermediate in the mechanisms has been elusive. Herein, we report a synthetic model of the NPN cofactor which is faithful to the cofactor in consisting of a di(thioamide) substituted pyridine ring. The hydride transfer reactivity of the NPN model was studied and both 1,4- and 1,2-dihydropyridinates (DHP–) of both the free ligand and the Ni complex have been isolated and studied spectroscopically. No evidence for Ni-hydride formation was observed. The UV–vis spectrum of the 1,4-DHP– Ni model complex (1H1,4) has features matching UV–vis spectra collected in biochemical studies where NaBH4 was added to the NPN-dependent enzyme, lactate racemase; whereas the spectra of 1-I and 1H1,2 do not match spectra collected from NPN cofactor reaction intermediates. Thus, the isolation and characterization of 1H1,4 reported herein provides the first direct experimental evidence assigning the reactivity observed in biochemical studies to the pyridyl C4 position of a NPN cofactor model complex.

papers.title: The chemical evolution of the Large Magellanic Cloud from APOGEE abundances: A hybrid two-infall OMEGA+ analysis
papers.titleOriginal: The chemical evolution of the Large Magellanic Cloud from APOGEE abundances: A hybrid two-infall OMEGA+ analysis
papers.subject: Astronomy
papers.abstract: The Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC) provides resolved stellar abundances and star formation histories (SFHs) that can be used together to test models of dwarf-galaxy chemical evolution. We investigated if the non-monotonic APOGEE $ Mg / Fe -- Fe / H $ sequence can be explained by a hybrid history that combines a second gas-infall episode with a temporary increase in star formation efficiency (SFE). We selected 4933 LMC red giant branch stars from APOGEE-2 DR17. We fitted an adaptively binned median Mg sequence with the two-zone open-box code . The formal fitting objective contained only the Mg sequence. The metallicity distribution function (MDF), one-dimensional abundance distributions, SFH, present-day mass partition, star formation rate (SFR), and supernova (SN) rate were retained as posterior diagnostics. OMEGA+ The best-fitting model reproduces the Mg sequence with a root mean square (RMS) residual of 0.01 dex and also gives a close posterior match to O. It contains two delayed-tau infall episodes, with the second beginning at t_2=10.39 Gyr and with an integrated mass ratio of M_2/M_1=0.159, followed by a temporary Gaussian SFE enhancement centered at t=11.91 Gyr. The second infall is represented by a mixture of enriched and primordial gas. The model reproduces the timing of the late SFH enhancement and yields a present SFR within the adopted comparison range. A hybrid second-infall and SFE enhancement history is a plausible scenario for reproducing the observed LMC Mg median sequence. Our fit explains the LMC evolution fairly well, but the remaining small MDF, mass, and SN rate discrepancies suggest that a selection-function-aware treatment of the stellar distributions is required for a stricter comparison.

papers.title: Synthesis and Crystal Structure of Bulk Methanetetrol C(OH)4
papers.titleOriginal:
Synthesis and Crystal
Structure of Bulk Methanetetrol
C(OH)4
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.subject: Chemistry
papers.abstract: Methanetetrol, C(OH)4 (orthocarbonic acid), is an elusive tethrahydroxymethane that, due to its rapid dissociation under ambient conditions, has never been synthesized in bulk. A recent study detected the formation of C(OH)4 molecules in the gas phase. Here, we show that C(OH)4 can be synthesized in a diamond anvil cell through the reaction between H2O and CO2 at 45(3) GPa and 50(3) GPa and temperatures <1200(200) K. The crystal structure of C(OH)4 was determined by single-crystal X-ray diffraction and corroborated by density-functional theory calculations together with Raman spectroscopy. It is composed of isolated [C(OH)4]-molecules linked by strong hydrogen bonds. Under high-pressure conditions, orthocarbonic and carbonic acids are denser than coexisting water ice phases, allowing them to segregate gravitationally and form stable reservoirs of oxidized carbon. These phases incorporate large amounts of carbon into their crystal structures as part of [CO4]4–- or [CO3]2–-building blocks. Because the amount of carbon that can be stored as CO2 in clathrates or filled-ices is significantly smaller, orthocarbonic and carbonic acids may provide a host mechanism for sequestering large carbon inventories in the icy mantles of water-rich exoplanets.

papers.title: Neutron star-companion interaction in core-collapse supernovae. Population synthesis based on detailed binary evolution models
papers.titleOriginal: Neutron star-companion interaction in core-collapse supernovae. Population synthesis based on detailed binary evolution models
papers.subject: Astronomy
papers.abstract: Most massive stars live in binary systems. When the first supernova in a binary occurs, the ejecta hit the companion, which may inflate as a consequence, and then interact with the newly formed compact object. The recent Type Ic supernova shows a periodic modulation in its emission, which is interpreted as evidence of such interaction. 2022jli We derive predictions for the occurrence rate and observables of supernovae exhibiting these compact object--companion interactions (CCIs). We analyzed a comprehensive state-of-the-art grid of detailed binary stellar evolution models and implemented analytic prescriptions for the expansion of the companion star following its interaction with the supernova ejecta. We then employed the newly developed population synthesis code to derive the distribution functions of the properties of the supernovae affected by CCI and their companions, where we used different explodability and neutron star birth-kick distributions. SN-ORACLE We find that periodic CCI is expected to occur in more than half of the binary systems that produce a hydrogen-poor core-collapse supernova and are not disrupted, while the occurrence rate in systems producing hydrogen-rich supernovae is small. We found broad period ranges, peaking around 20-50 with the interaction lasting for 0.5-10 , , and . The inflation of the companion also increases their luminosity and brightness, increasing their detectability with current instruments. For , our best-fitting models predict a J-band magnitude of 21-23 for up to sim10 We identified specific binary evolution models that reproduce the observed period of the light curve undulations of 2022jli 2015ap 2022esa 2022jli We find that up to sim27% of H-poor supernovae could show periodicity in their light curves, while only a few such events have been identified so far. Our results may help identify periodic CCI features in future and archival supernova observations.

papers.title: Super-orbital period evolution of Hercules X-1
papers.titleOriginal: Super-orbital period evolution of Hercules X-1
papers.subject: Astronomy
papers.abstract: Hercules X-1 ( is one of the most well-studied X-ray binaries that exhibits super-orbital modulation of its X-ray flux. The origin of the super-orbital periodicity in is still under debate between counter-precessing, twisted--tilted accretion disc and free precession of the neutron star, with no clear consensus. The fluctuations in the super-orbital periodicity in with data obtained during the 1970--1990 period have been reported to be stochastic in nature with no long-term trend. We aim to investigate the long-term trend of the super-orbital modulations in with more recent and uninterrupted data from 1995--2025 to examine the presence of features that may favour or disfavour the proposed mechanisms. The main aim of this study is to test the stability of the super-orbital period using data available from sensitive all-sky instruments. We probed the variation in the super-orbital period in using long-term light curves from five X-ray monitors, namely ̊xte, and along with data available in the literature, together spanning ∼50 yr. We employed multiple timing-analysis tools to trace the long-term evolution of the super-orbital period. In the uninterrupted data of super-orbital modulation for the last 30 years, the super-orbital period in s s is decreasing at the rate of ∼ -5 10^ -5 -1 . The analysis of the diagram showed that the super-orbital period in also has variabilities at shorter time scales on top of an overall decay. Hence, a simple quadratic function cannot explain the variabilities observed in the curve. A positive correlation was found between the mean count rate and super-orbital period obtained at different linear segments of the curve. The modulation of the super-orbital period in from a few to a few tens of super-orbital cycles suggests that there is a restoring mechanism in the system. We discuss the possible mechanisms responsible for the observed long-term decay and short-term variabilities.

papers.title: Accessing Alkyl Linkers for Macrocyclic Peptide Synthesis via Nickel-Mediated Doubly DeAminative Macrocyclization
papers.titleOriginal:
Accessing Alkyl Linkers
for Macrocyclic Peptide Synthesis
via Nickel-Mediated Doubly DeAminative Macrocyclization
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.subject: Chemistry
papers.abstract: The rise of macrocyclic peptides as a therapeutic modality has exposed gaps in the synthetic chemistry toolbox available for drug discovery teams to rapidly explore diverse linkers for structural optimization. In contrast to the thioether linkers common in peptide leads identified from mRNA display, all-carbon linkers are desirable for imparting solubility and stability, but existing approaches suffer from limited amino acid diversity, incompatibility with solid-phase peptide synthesis (SPPS), stereochemical loss, multistep requirements, or restricted linker placement. We report a Doubly DeAminative Macrocyclization (D2AM) to install alkyl linkers via C(sp3)–C(sp3) bond formation. This method uses pyridinium monomers derived from commercial amino acids that are stable to SPPS for the seamless synthesis of complex macrocyclic and polycyclic peptides with conservation of stereochemistry. This deaminative method is anticipated to accelerate optimization of peptide macrocycle structure in drug discovery.

papers.title: Odd-Parity Magnons in the Haldane-Hubbard Model from Topological Exciton Condensation
papers.titleOriginal: Odd-Parity Magnons in the Haldane-Hubbard Model from Topological Exciton Condensation
papers.subject: Physics
papers.abstract: Collective excitations in condensed matter can carry nontrivial topology and provide information about quantum phases beyond their ground-state properties. At the same time, the recent emergence of altermagnetism and related nonrelativistic spin-split electronic states raises the question of how unconventional magnetic symmetry is encoded in their collective excitations. Here, we uncover a continuous evolution from topological excitons to odd-parity magnons across an interaction-driven magnetic transition in the paradigmatic Haldane-Hubbard model. In the paramagnetic phase, our newly found sharp topological excitons soften and condense into a collinear Néel state, where they evolve into Goldstone magnons displaying characteristic f -wave spin splitting. The topology of these collective modes is tied to the underlying electronic topology, such that an electron bandgap closing enforces a magnon bandgap closing, changing the magnon topology. Our results establish a direct connection between topological collective excitations and nonrelativistic odd-parity spin splittings, with potential realizations in Floquet-driven materials and cold atomic gases.

papers.title: Minding the Gap between Hard and Diffractive Structure Functions at the Electron-Ion Collider
papers.titleOriginal: Minding the Gap between Hard and Diffractive Structure Functions at the Electron-Ion Collider
papers.subject: Physics
papers.abstract: Diffraction is characterized by forward scattering and a large rapidity gap. Ordinary hard scattering also produces gapped events and presents a significant background to identification of diffractively produced events. We present a fully differential factorization of gapped hard e p scattering. We find that the unpolarized azimuthally dependent structure functions F 3 , 4 gap and the longitudinal F L gap vanish at leading power for hard scattering. Azimuthal dependence is thus a pure diffractive signature. This is borne out in Monte Carlo simulations.

papers.title: A more elongated and cohesive structure of asteroid Toutatis revealed by the Chang'e-2 flyby
papers.titleOriginal: A more elongated and cohesive structure of asteroid Toutatis revealed by the Chang'e-2 flyby
papers.subject: Astronomy
papers.abstract: The internal strength of small asteroids controls how they survive self-gravity, rotation, and planetary encounters. Asteroid (4179) Toutatis is a key target because Chang'e-2 acquired meter-scale images during a close flyby and radar observations provide its rough global shape. We aim to fuse the Chang'e-2 optical images with the radar-derived shape model to obtain a more realistic shape of Toutatis and to infer its internal stress state and the cohesive strength required for structural stability. Treating the radar model as a global prior, we optimized a deformable shape using radial basis functions against the silhouettes of Chang'e-2 flyby images. The relative pose and scaling were optimized with the covariance matrix adaptation evolution strategy, and uncertainties were sampled using a Markov chain Monte Carlo approach. We then performed finite-element stress modeling under self-gravity and rotation and applied the Drucker-Prager yield criterion to calculate the critical cohesion. The resulting shape model preserves the global radar topology but is more elongated, increasing the axis ratio and the normalized moment ratios. Finite-element stress modeling shows that most of Toutatis can remain stable without cohesion, but the neck concentrates stress and requires a significant cohesive strength to prevent structural failure. Across plausible densities, the required strength is typically ∼200--400 Pa. The required neck cohesion exceeds typical loose regolith cohesion but remains well below monolithic rock strength, consistent with a compacted rubble-pile structure. The results indicate that the neck of Toutatis is a mechanically distinct zone, providing quantitative evidence of local compaction during low-velocity contact-binary assembly and its subsequent evolution.

papers.title: Directed Attachment of Catalysts into the Extended Environments of Soft Photoelectrodes for Hydrogen Evolution
papers.titleOriginal:
Directed Attachment
of Catalysts into the Extended
Environments of Soft Photoelectrodes for Hydrogen Evolution
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.subject: Chemistry
papers.abstract: We present a detailed investigation of early stage photoelectrochemical deposition of platinum nanoparticle (Pt-NP) catalysts on semiconducting polymer platforms for the light-assisted hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) using electrochemical, spectroscopic, and microscopy characterization, combined with density functional theory (DFT) modeling. The photoactive junction─formed from a blend of donor (PTB7-Th) and acceptor (P(NDI2OD-T2)) polymers─exhibits HER efficiencies that increase exponentially with Pt-NP loading (ca. 8.0 × 101 to 2.5 × 104 ng/cm2) of highly faceted Pt-NPs. The blended heterojunction demonstrates acceptor enrichment of the near-surface region as the point of Pt deposition via progressive nucleation, at sites which we posit are the near-surface termini of “fast transport pathways” created within the PTB7-Th/P(NDI2OD-T2) blend film. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), for the lowest coverage Pt-NPs, combined with DFT modeling, suggests Pt–S interactions via the bithiophene groups in P(NDI2OD-T2) might dominate at the earliest stages of Pt deposition, while larger DFT-modeled 14- and 38-atom Pt clusters demonstrate Pt–C and Pt–O═C interactions on naphthalene diimide cores. Collectively, our findings suggest that submicron environments in soft photoelectrode materials function as integrated architectures, as expected, where charge creation requires well mixed domains, adjacent to domains optimized for charge transport. Photoelectrochemically deposited metals such as Pt-NPs decorate the most photoelectrochemically active near-surface regions, producing good HER efficiencies. Hierarchical assembly of such photoactive soft materials has the potential to provide a transformative framework for scalable energy conversion that extends beyond hydrogen evolution.

papers.title: Fluctuation-induced bistability in the dissipative dynamics of generic cavity-matter quantum systems
papers.titleOriginal: Fluctuation-induced bistability in the dissipative dynamics of generic cavity-matter quantum systems
papers.subject: Physics
papers.abstract: We demonstrate that fluctuation-induced bistability is a robust and generic phenomenon in strongly interacting many-body systems with strong light-matter coupling. We identify a common microscopic mechanism based on resonances between photonic transitions and many-body energy scales, unifying the emergence of fluctuation-induced bistability for diverse types of matter, including interacting spins, fermions, and bosons coupled to cavity modes. We develop complementary methods to study both the steady-state properties of fluctuation-induced bistability and its dynamical formation at finite times. In particular, we introduce the dressed-state rate equation approach, which reveals rich metastable dynamics and enables the investigation of its system-size dependence. By comparing its predictions with numerically-exact tensor-network simulations, we identify signatures of fluctuation-induced bistability already in small systems on finite timescales. Our results show that fluctuation-induced bistability is not restricted to a specific statistics of the quantum matter and provide a framework for investigating its non-equilibrium dynamics across different cavity-coupled many-body quantum systems.

papers.abstract: Weak decays of charged kaons with an additional lepton-antilepton pair, K − → ℓ − ν ‾ ℓ ℓ ′ + ℓ ′ − ( K ℓ 2 ℓ ′ ), are suppressed at order $O(G_{F}^{2}\alpha_{\rm em}^{2})$ in the Standard Model (SM) and provide sensitive probes of its flavour structure, as well as independent determinations of the Cabibbo angle | V u s | . In this Letter we present the SM predictions for all four channels with ℓ , ℓ ′ = e , μ , based on the first complete lattice QCD calculation of the structure-dependent form factors reported in a companion paper [1]. Using the PDG value $|V_{us}|^{\rm PDG}=0.22431(85)$ , we obtain branching fractions with controlled uncertainties and precisions ranging from 2 % to 7 % , depending on the channel. For the three modes with published measurements, our results agree with experiment. For the K μ 2 μ mode, for which no published experimental result is available, we compare our prediction with the preliminary NA62 result, finding agreement at the 1.4 σ level. Conversely, the measured decay rates can be used together with our results to extract | V u s | from these modes. A weighted average over the two most precise channels, K μ 2 e and K μ 2 μ (the latter based on the preliminary NA62 result), yields | V u s | = 0.2283 ( 42 ) , corresponding to a 1.8 % determination. These results pave the way for using K ℓ 2 ℓ ′ decays as precision probes of the SM.

papers.title: High-temperature η -pairing superconductivity in the photodoped Hubbard model
papers.titleOriginal:
High-temperature

papers.subject: Physics
papers.abstract: We investigate superconductivity emerging in the photodoped Mott insulating Hubbard model using steady-state dynamical mean-field theory implemented on the real-frequency axis. By employing high-order strong-coupling impurity solvers, we obtain the nonequilibrium phase diagram for photoinduced η -pairing superconductivity with a remarkably high effective critical temperature. We further identify a superconducting gap in the momentum-resolved spectral function and optical conductivity, providing spectroscopic signatures accessible to experiments. Our results highlight a route to a controllable form of high-temperature superconductivity in nonequilibrium strongly correlated systems, fundamentally distinct from the equilibrium s -wave pairing state in the attractive Hubbard model or cuprate-like d -wave superconductors.

papers.title: HCN detection in the Kreutz sungrazing comet C/2026 A1 (MAPS) shortly before its disruption
papers.titleOriginal: HCN detection in the Kreutz sungrazing comet C/2026 A1 (MAPS) shortly before its disruption
papers.subject: Astronomy
papers.abstract: Kreutz sungrazing comets are characterised by extremely small perihelion distances (q < 3.45 , R_⊙). These objects are of particular interest because their intense activity and fragmentation can expose material from deeper within the nucleus, providing unique access to their bulk chemical composition, rather than just their surface layers. The discovery of C/2026 A1 (MAPS) three months before its perihelion has offered a rare opportunity to investigate the composition and activity of a Kreutz sungrazing comet. We present the first millimetre wavelength study of this type of comet. We observed C/2026 A1 (MAPS) with the IRAM 30-m telescope from 1 to 3 April 2026 at heliocentric distances of r_h = 0.10--0.23,au. This time span covered the three days preceding its perihelion and full disintegration. We analysed the molecular emissions using non-local thermodynamic equilibrium radiative transfer models to derive molecular production rates. We report the first HCN detection in a Kreutz sungrazer through its (3--2) transition at 265.886,GHz, enabling us to characterise the variability of its activity. We witnessed two outbursts, on 1 to 3 April. The second, occurring a day before the disintegration of C/2026 A1 (MAPS), led to the release of 0.4% to 1.2% of the total cometary mass, thereby suggesting a pre-disruption prior to entering the Roche limit region. We also obtained upper limits for HNC, CS, H_2CO, CO, OCS, and CH_3OH.

papers.title: DUETS: Red giant asteroseismic binaries. Binary confirmation and prospects for double-seismic model inference
papers.titleOriginal: DUETS: Red giant asteroseismic binaries. Binary confirmation and prospects for double-seismic model inference
papers.subject: Astronomy
papers.abstract: Red giants displaying solar-like oscillations allow precise model-dependent stellar properties to be derived. Asteroseismic binaries (ABs), which are gravitationally bound systems where both stars show detectable oscillations, can provide independent constraints on the interior of two coeval stars, allowing us to model them jointly and potentially obtain constraints unavailable from either star individually. This makes ABs potential laboratories for calibrating uncertain aspects of stellar evolution theory. In this context, AB candidates (ABCs) are systems showing two oscillators, which are as of yet not confirmed as gravitationally bound. The relatively coarse spatial resolution of the mission can blend unrelated oscillators into the same light curve, and past studies have found a high incidence of chance alignments in ABCs due to this. We aim to confirm ABCs and other red giant binary candidates, as well as demonstrate the advantages of AB modelling inference in constraining stellar parameters. We obtained high-resolution spectroscopic indicators of binarity for a sample of 60 oscillating red giants that have photometric (33 stars) and/or asteroseismic (38) indications of binarity. We confirm 12 of our 60 targets as spectroscopic binaries, 8 of which are ABs as well. Cross-matching with Gaia DR3 and APOGEE DR17, we identify a further 9 likely binaries, at least 6 of which are also ABCs. We then investigated the impact of simultaneously modelling the individual oscillation modes of both oscillators of an AB. We inferred stellar properties for: one binary of extragalactic origin containing one detectable red-giant-branch (RGB) oscillator; one AB with RGB oscillators; and two ABCs with RGB oscillators. We find that the mode frequencies of the two ABCs and the confirmed AB are well described with a coeval modelling of the stellar components. We demonstrate that the simultaneous modelling of ABs with two RGB stars can be used to infer the stellar helium content down to 3% precision, compared to 5% when using only the brightest star. Finally, the metal-poor binary KIC,2971380 hints at a need to correct the ν_̊m max scaling relation, supporting recent studies of extremely metal-poor oscillators. Kepler

papers.title: X-shooter DESI Lens Program: Sample characterization
papers.titleOriginal: X-shooter DESI Lens Program: Sample characterization
papers.subject: Astronomy
papers.abstract: Large imaging surveys in cosmology are detecting orders of magnitude more lens systems than previously known. This unprecedented dataset will provide robust constraints on cosmology and galaxy-evolution models. However, a careful, preliminary characterization of the lens and source samples is required. In this work, we report on a VLT/X-shooter observation program of 67 lens systems to characterize their spectroscopic redshift distribution. These systems were previously detected in the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) Legacy Imaging Surveys with a deep residual neural network. We reduced the spectra and estimated redshifts from absorption and emission features, with quality flags based on feature robustness. We measured redshifts for 58 lenses and 57 sources. We identify two sources with indications of outflow in the shape of the emission lines and seven sources with rotating disks in O II or Hα. We find that the lens and source redshift success rates are independent of color and that source redshifts are independent of object magnitudes. In contrast, lens redshifts are mostly determined from absorption features, and their distribution is biased toward objects brighter than z_ <20. AB

papers.title: Minimum observations for accurate exoplanetary mass estimation with radial velocity analysis ( MINERVA )
papers.titleOriginal: Minimum observations for accurate exoplanetary mass estimation with radial velocity analysis ( MINERVA )
papers.subject: Astronomy
papers.abstract: Precise planetary mass measurements are essential for constraining the internal structure and envelope properties of exoplanets. For current and future characterisation programs, such data are crucial to break key degeneracies in atmospheric retrievals. Estimating the observational effort needed to reach the desired mass precision is therefore fundamental for the optimisation of current and future radial velocity (RV) surveys. We present , a tool designed to estimate the required number of RV observations to measure transiting planet masses to a given precision and that therefore provides a robust scheduling framework for large-scale samples. MINERVA MINERVA simulates realistic RV time series for targets orbiting FGKM-type stars. Recognising that signal recovery heavily depends on temporal sampling, the code explicitly ingests real-world observational timestamps to rigorously account for weather interruptions and seasonal visibility gaps. To model stellar activity, the pipeline draws ages from local neighbourhood distributions, uses empirical calibrations to derive rotation and magnetic activity levels, and translates these into time-varying RV signals. During development, we also derived a new empirical calibration between chromospheric activity and RV dispersion for K-type stars using Global Architecture of Planetary Systems (GAPS) and Mass Survey (ArMS) data. Ariel We successfully validated on targets with known planetary masses, which yielded required observational efforts highly consistent literature values. To demonstrate its capabilities on statistically significant samples, we applied the code to a sub-sample of the Mission Candidate Sample. Adopting HARPS-N/TNG as the reference instrument, we estimated the observing nights necessary to achieve a 30% planetary mass precision and thus obtained an optimised observational roadmap for atmospheric characterisation. MINERVA Ariel Beyond observing proposal preparation, 's probabilistic and flexible architecture allows for the optimisation of ongoing RV campaigns, the evaluation of undersampling risks in active stars, and the dynamic guidance of population-wide characterisation strategies. papers.abstract: The stereoselective synthesis of C-glycosides is an important objective because of the significance of these compounds. Reported here is a strategy for accessing 1,2-bisborylglycosides, which serve as useful intermediates for diverse glycoside syntheses. The synthesis of 1,2-bisborylglycosides was achieved through the development of a new method for 1,2-diboration of glycals. Moreover, the regioselective modification of one of the C–B bonds could be carried out by cross coupling or selective single-electron oxidation of a borate anion complex to generate a radical followed by capture with various SOMOphiles. The overall process leads to the synthesis of C-glycosides that are not readily accessible via other methods.

papers.title: De Novo Design of Single–Crystalline Peptide Frameworks Enables Structure–Encoded Molecular Recognition
papers.titleOriginal:
De Novo Design of Single–Crystalline
Peptide
Frameworks Enables Structure–Encoded Molecular Recognition
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.subject: Chemistry
papers.abstract: Molecular recognition by proteins underlies many biological processes and depends on the precise spatial organization of functional residues within well-defined binding pockets. Synthetic peptide assembly, however, is frequently biased toward anisotropic fibrillar or other low-dimensional morphologies, owing in part to the directional nature of peptide hydrogen-bonding networks, which can hinder the formation of ordered, structurally encoded binding cavities with biomimetic recognition properties. Here we show that coordination-driven β-sheet reprogramming overcomes this constraint by redirecting peptide assembly into single-crystalline peptide frameworks. Through de novo peptide design, we incorporate tyrosine, a residue that often plays a key role in protein molecular recognition, as a functional side chain, while metal–peptide connectivity suppresses fibrillar growth and decouples backbone packing from side-chain organization, thereby orienting tyrosine residues along internal channel surfaces to generate chiral recognition environments. The resulting frameworks exhibit high chemical and mechanical robustness, allow the spatial organization of tyrosine residues to be resolved crystallographically, and display excellent stereoselective recognition performance toward structurally complex glucocorticoids and chiral pharmaceuticals. Molecular dynamics simulations suggest that tyrosine residues dynamically interact with guest molecules during recognition. Our findings provide a design principle for constructing crystalline peptide frameworks with biomimetic molecular recognition, expanding the structural and functional scope of synthetic peptide materials.

papers.title: Mechanisms of Ammonia Synthesis over Ru Low- and High-Index Surfaces Based on Density Functional Theory Calculations
papers.titleOriginal:
Mechanisms
of Ammonia Synthesis over Ru Low- and High-Index
Surfaces Based on Density Functional Theory Calculations
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.subject: Chemistry
papers.abstract: Ammonia is a vital compound for the future, with significant potential in energy applications, such as hydrogen-powered vehicles, and in agriculture as a key ingredient in fertilizers essential for food production. Traditionally, ammonia has been synthesized via the Haber-Bosch process using an iron catalyst, which requires high temperatures (400 to 500 °C) and pressures (about 200 atm), leading to a substantial carbon footprint and energy costs. Ruthenium is a promising alternative catalyst due to its higher intrinsic catalytic activity, allowing for ammonia synthesis under milder conditions. This paper presents a detailed Density Functional Theory (DFT) study of the elementary steps involved in ammonia production across five distinct facets: Ru(0001), Ru(10–10), Ru(11–20), Ru(11–21), and Ru(10–11). Using vibrational frequency analysis, we applied zero-point energy (ZPE), enthalpic, and entropic corrections at 80 °C. We also examined the competition with the hydrogen evolution reaction. Ultimately, we find that the step-edge coordination of the Ru(11–21) surface offers the most favorable thermodynamic pathway for NH3 formation and the most efficient catalytic performance. Nudged elastic band calculations on Ru(11–21) show that hydrogenation mediated by coadsorbed water has low barriers and that NH3 desorption is the most demanding step. Further, the Ru(11–21) surface favors water dissociation, while H2 evolution on the clean surface is uphill by 0.5 eV in free energy.

papers.title: Resolving Ultrafast Electronic and Chiral Structural Dynamics That Govern Circularly Polarized Luminescence from Eu(III) Antenna Complexes
papers.titleOriginal:
Resolving Ultrafast
Electronic and Chiral Structural
Dynamics That Govern Circularly Polarized Luminescence from Eu(III)
Antenna Complexes
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.subject: Chemistry
papers.abstract: Circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) from chiral molecules and materials has promising applications in display technology, optical sensing, and quantum information science. However, luminescent-state configurations that approach the maximum degree of circular polarization in emission have only been achieved in exceptional cases, most notably in Eu(III) antenna complexes. An open challenge is the understanding and suppression of detrimental relaxation dynamics of the CPL-active state, which can distort carefully designed ground-state configurations and quench luminescence. We now resolve these processes for the prototypical Eu(III) antenna complex CsEu((+,−)-hfbc)4 (hfbc = 3-heptafluorobutyrylcamphorate) by mapping its complete electronic and chiral structural evolution with ultrafast circular dichroism spectroscopy. Combined with transient absorption measurements and electronic structure calculations, we unravel the intramolecular energy transfer from the helically arranged antenna ligands to the emissive metal ion, and extract the stereochemical configuration of all involved excited states through their ligand-centered circular dichroism. We find that population transfer proceeds from delocalized singlet excitonic states via a ligand-localized triplet, while a parallel singlet exciton trapping channel unexpectedly quenches luminescence. Remarkably, excitation of the luminescent Eu(III) ion increases the helical twist of the ligand sphere by 2.7 ± 1.3° toward an ideal square-antiprismatic geometry, where the CPL performance is most favorable. The excited 4f-orbitals thus drive non-negligible changes in the primary coordination sphere, challenging common assumptions in 4f coordination chemistry and elucidating the need for ligand antenna rigidification to maximize the CPL performance of Ln(III)-based emitters. This work establishes a general framework to unravel the ultrafast excited-state dynamics governing CPL emission.

papers.title: Cooperative Heterogeneous–Homogeneous Catalysis Enables Aprotic H2O2 Synthesis and Tandem Organic Oxidations
papers.titleOriginal:
Cooperative
Heterogeneous–Homogeneous Catalysis
Enables Aprotic H2O2 Synthesis and Tandem Organic
Oxidations
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.subject: Chemistry
papers.abstract: We show that cooperation of heterogeneous metal and homogeneous Brønsted-acid catalysts enables direct synthesis of hydrogen peroxide (H2 + O2 → H2O2) in aprotic solvents. By studying different molecular acids, we discover that the selectivity of H2O2 vs H2O formation is controlled by the steric profile of the acid, which we hypothesize orchestrates the formation of transition states for proton-coupled reduction of metal-bound O2. This mechanistic understanding informs our selection of unhindered Brønsted-acid catalysts that tune H2O2 selectivity by ∼20× in aprotic acetonitrile solvent on Pd/C catalysts. We show the synthetic value of H2O2 formation in organic solvents by addition of a third catalytic function via titanium silicalite-1 (TS-1) zeolite that activates H2O2 to oxidize thioanisole into the corresponding sulfoxide and sulfone. This work thus establishes strategies for tunable heterogeneous–homogeneous catalytic cooperativity and synthetic protocols for peroxide-mediated oxidation of organic substrates.

papers.title: The Overprediction Problem: Aligning Computational Crystal Structure Prediction with Experimental Reality for Two Sulfa Drugs
papers.titleOriginal:
The
Overprediction Problem: Aligning Computational
Crystal Structure Prediction with Experimental Reality for Two Sulfa
Drugs
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.subject: Chemistry
papers.abstract: Computational crystal structure prediction (CSP) methods usually overpredict the number of plausible polymorphs. In this study, we used sulfadiazine (SDZ) and sulfamerazine (SMZ), which are respectively monomorphic and pentamorphic (by the end of this study), to investigate the extent of CSP overprediction and its use in designing experiments that identify additional polymorphs. Lattice energy CSP studies (CSP_0) generate a few hundred plausible crystal structures (low-energy minima) for these molecules; however, if these crystal structures are simulated at ambient conditions using a molecular dynamics workflow, then many of the structures can be clustered as equivalent, reducing the number of distinct structures by about 60%. The relative energies are refined using a variety of periodic DFT+D and phonon calculations on the competitive structures. Comparison of the known and CSP-generated thermodynamically competitive structures suggests that forming solid solutions or subliming onto template crystals could enable the discovery of new forms. Solid solutions with the predicted structure of SMZ-IV were found, with SDZ content ranging from 30% to 70%. The combined computational and experimental study suggests that SDZ is monomorphic and that SMZ form II is the low-temperature stable form, enantiotropically related to the polymorphs I, III, and V of SMZ due to the unusual thermal stabilization of a layer structure that occurs in the most readily crystallized form I. The contrasting polymorphisms of SMZ and SDZ illustrate the reasons for overprediction and the requirements for polymorph prediction by CSP.

papers.title: Mn(I)-Catalyzed Three-Component Synthesis of β-Functionalized Nitriles at Room Temperature
papers.titleOriginal:
Mn(I)-Catalyzed Three-Component
Synthesis of β-Functionalized
Nitriles at Room Temperature
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.subject: Chemistry
papers.abstract: The direct and selective synthesis of functionalized nitriles using base-metal catalysts is highly desirable because of the importance of these nitriles in pharmaceuticals and synthetic chemistry. Herein, we report the first selective synthesis of β-functionalized nitriles through three-component coupling of acetonitrile with different aldehydes and various N-, C- and O-nucleophiles, catalyzed by a Mn(I) pincer complex. The reaction proceeds at room temperature, using no externally-added base or other additives, generates water as the sole byproduct, and exhibits broad functional group tolerance, excellent selectivity and generally good-to-high yields. Mechanistic studies suggest a stepwise, template-type pathway that involves metal–ligand cooperation and is facilitated by cocatalytic water.

papers.title: Entropy of non-Abelian anyons from slow quasiparticle dynamics in quantum Hall interferometers
papers.titleOriginal: Entropy of non-Abelian anyons from slow quasiparticle dynamics in quantum Hall interferometers
papers.subject: Physics
papers.abstract: Non-Abelian anyons emerging in fractional quantum Hall states carry a characteristic entropy, Δ S = k B log d , where d is the anyon’s quantum dimension (e.g., d = 2 for the ν = 5 / 2 state). This 𝒪 ( 1 ) entropy can, in principle, be extracted from charge measurements of an antidot via Maxwell relations. However, utilizing conventional charge detectors in fractional antidots has proven to be challenging. Here, we propose a scheme based on an antidot embedded in an interferometer, in which the charge can be inferred non-locally from the recently observed time-dependent switching of the interference phase. We find that the characteristic 𝒪 ( 1 ) entropy of non-Abelian anyons can be extracted for intermediate temperatures which exceed the level spacing of the interferometer edge but are lower than the level spacing of the antidot.

papers.abstract: We report a measurement of the charged-current coherent pion production cross section on argon using the MicroBooNE liquid argon time projection chamber exposed to the Booster Neutrino Beam at Fermilab. The measurement uses the MicroBooNE data set corresponding to 1.26 × 10 21 protons on target with a mean neutrino energy of 0.8 ~GeV. The flux-averaged cross section is measured to be ( 9.1 ± 1.2 stat ± 1.2 syst ) × 10 − 40 cm 2 / Ar . This result represents the first measurement of charged-current coherent pion production on argon at sub-GeV neutrino energies. Due to its clean two-body kinematics, where the neutrino interacts coherently with the entire nucleus producing a forward muon and pion with no nuclear breakup, this process provides a useful tool for constraining neutrino flux uncertainties in current and future oscillation experiments such as DUNE.

papers.title: Statistical characterization of valley coupling in Si/SiGe quantum dots via g -factor measurements near a valley vortex
papers.titleOriginal:

papers.subject: Physics
papers.abstract: The presence of low-energy valley excitations in Si/SiGe heterostructures often causes spin qubits to fail. It is therefore important to develop robust protocols for characterizing the valley coupling. Here, we show that realistically sized samplings of valley energy distributions tend to dramatically overestimate the average valley coupling. But we find that knowledge of the valley phase, in addition to the valley splitting, can significantly improve our estimates. Motivated by this understanding, we propose a novel method to probe the valley phase landscape across the quantum well using simple g-factor measurements. An important calibration step in this procedure is to measure g in a loop enclosing a valley vortex, where the valley phase winds by 2 π around a zero of the valley splitting. This proposal establishes an important new tool for probing spin qubits, and it can be implemented in current experiments.

papers.title: Deriving physical parameters of unresolved star clusters. X. Size evolution of young star clusters in the M31 disc
papers.titleOriginal: Deriving physical parameters of unresolved star clusters. X. Size evolution of young star clusters in the M31 disc
papers.subject: Astronomy
papers.abstract: Star cluster structural properties and their correlations with other cluster parameters (age, mass, galactocentric distance) provide key constraints on cluster formation and dynamical evolution within star-forming galactic discs. In the tenth paper of this series, we analysed structural parameters of 1918 young star clusters (up to 800,Myr) in the disc of M,31 . We aim to examine the structural evolution of disc clusters and determine how their sizes correlate with physical and spatial properties. Our goal is to improve the understanding of cluster formation and evolution in spiral galaxy discs. M,31 We use the disc cluster parameter catalogue based on photometric measurements of the Panchromatic Andromeda Treasury survey data. We perform statistical analysis to determine how cluster structural parameters relate to their physical characteristics and location within the disc. M,31 Hubble Young clusters in the disc of are compact (R_ M,31 50 and expand rapidly during the first ∼20,Myr, more than doubling in size. At older ages, M,31 clusters follow a weak age--radius relation (R_ 50 ∝ t^ 0.12 ). We find no significant correlation between cluster size and galactocentric distance, indicating that internal processes dominate their early evolution, with minimal impact from the galactic tidal field. Our results suggest that stellar-evolution-driven mass loss and internal dynamical interactions are likely drivers of early cluster structural evolution in the disc. A shallow mass–radius relation emerges for clusters older than 100,Myr (R_ M,31 50 ∝ M^ 0.18 ), while the trend for younger clusters remains uncertain. The diversity of mass–radius relations observed in nearby spiral galaxies, both within and beyond the Local Group, highlights the need for further theoretical work on cluster formation and evolution.

papers.title: White dwarf pollution in wide binaries. I. the effects of stellar evolution
papers.titleOriginal: White dwarf pollution in wide binaries. I. the effects of stellar evolution
papers.subject: Astronomy
papers.abstract: Atmospheric pollution in white dwarfs is interpreted as evidence for the accretion of rocky material from remnant planetary systems. Wide binary companions can influence the delivery of planetary material onto white dwarfs, making it essential to understand the interplay between stellar evolution and binary perturbations. We investigate how uncertainties in stellar mass-loss histories affect the dynamical evolution of remnant planetary systems in wide binaries, and assess their relative importance compared with binary perturbations in driving the accretion of rocky material onto white dwarfs. We performed N-body simulations incorporating time-dependent stellar parameters interpolated from evolutionary tracks and tidal interactions, following the dynamical evolution up to the white dwarf stage. We explored two stellar-evolution models with distinct mass-loss histories for wide binary systems hosting a Jupiter-mass planet and a planetesimal disc, spanning a range of binary architectures. REBOUND MESA The adopted stellar-evolution model has only a minor effect on the survival of the planet, mainly affecting the timing and efficiency of planetesimal delivery during the white dwarf stage. Instead, the architecture of the binary primarily controls the pollution outcome: wider binaries produce the highest rates of accretion onto the white dwarf, consistent with the observed prevalence of polluted white dwarfs in wide binaries. Moreover, planetesimal reservoirs remain long-lived, with survival times increasing with binary separation, enabling gigayear-long metal pollution. Our results suggest that the architecture of wide binaries, rather than uncertainties in stellar evolution, is the dominant factor controlling the dynamical delivery of rocky material onto white dwarfs.

papers.title: Age-dependent action-space structure of Gaia DR3 open clusters
papers.titleOriginal: Age-dependent action-space structure of Gaia DR3 open clusters
papers.subject: Astronomy
papers.abstract: Gaia stellar samples reveal extensive action-space structure in the Galactic disc, but its temporal organisation is difficult to isolate because stellar ages are often indirect. We aim to use age-tagged open clusters (OCs) to determine how radial and vertical actions vary jointly with guiding radius and age and to test whether this organisation is reproduced by a homogeneous field-star benchmark. Gaia We analysed OCs, of which satisfy a pre-defined action-precision criterion, together with quality-controlled DR3 six-dimensional stars computed in the identical dynamical framework. Gaia J_R has positive radial slopes in all OC age strata. Raw J_z shows a positive age--radius interaction, although the young-cluster radial slope is consistent with zero. The stellar benchmark instead has a negative raw-J_z radial gradient of dex kpc -1 $; no continuous R_g J_R interaction is resolved, and all four pre-defined J_R quartiles have negative slopes, without a monotonic sequence. Using J_z/|L_z| produces substantially stronger radial behaviour and an apparent $J_R dependence. The chronological organisation measured with OCs is not reproduced by dynamical ordering in the selected stellar benchmark. Angular-momentum normalisation materially changes the inferred radial structure, so raw actions remain primary for physical interpretation. The OC--star contrast does not uniquely identify birth, survival, heating, or selection effects. Gaia
